summary: This excerpt from a novel, labeled 'Book 11 — part 99', shows schoolgirls at a school talking in a study hour. Huldah complains that she lost her Latin grammar after a quarrel with Herbert Dunn, whom she has stopped speaking to and whose class pin she returned. Rebecca defends Miss Maxwell, the teacher Huldah disparages, while Emma Jane tries to end the discussion. The passage also describes Huldah's flashy outfit and her pins, and mentions a handsome stranger in the principal's office.
one_line: Schoolgirls in a study hour discuss Miss Maxwell, a lost Latin grammar, and Huldah's quarrel with Herbert Dunn.
key_facts: Huldah says she wanted to tell Miss Maxwell that it was her place to teach her Latin, not manners.
Rebecca tells Huldah she wishes she would not talk against Miss Maxwell, and says, "I not only abide, I love her!"
Rebecca says she would like to put a marble platform in Miss Maxwell's class-room and have her sit in a velvet chair behind a golden table.
Emma Jane interrupts the argument by asking whether Huldah's study hour is now.
Huldah says she lost her Latin grammar yesterday after leaving it in the hall for half an hour.
Huldah had a regular scene with Herbert Dunn, had not spoken to him for a week, and gave him back his class pin.
Mr. Morrison thinks the grammar will be returned and has lent Huldah another copy.
Huldah wears a woolen dress that was once gray but was dyed a brilliant blue.
Huldah added three rows of white braid and large white pearl buttons to her gray jacket to make it more "dressy."
Her gray felt hat has a white feather, and a white tissue veil with large black dots.
Rebecca notes that the front of Huldah's red hair has been dulled by incessant frizzing with curling irons.
Huldah's open jacket shows a small American flag, a button of the Wareham Rowing Club, and one or two society pins.
Huldah hoped the girls would ask whose ring she was wearing this week.
Huldah describes a perfectly elegant gentleman in the principal's office, a stranger to her, who was too young to be a father of the girls and too old to be a brother.
Huldah says that she wishes the stranger was a new teacher, but there is no such luck.
